mission: For each competitor in {n8n, Temporal, Camunda, Argo}, identify strengths, where Oyatie lacks, and measurable patches for specs/products/workflow.json.

source_policy.claim_rule: Competitor claims in this artifact must cite source_evidence ids; Oyatie target metrics are internal goals and must be bench-proven before launch.

source_evidence.claim: n8n is a workflow automation tool combining AI capabilities with business process automation; it emphasizes app/API connection, customization, npm/Docker/cloud options, and self-host privacy.

n8n queue mode splits main/webhook handling from workers through Redis and a database; workers execute jobs, write results, and can expose health/readiness/metrics endpoints; queue mode does not support filesystem binary data and recommends Postgres over SQLite.
n8n supports production execution concurrency limits and FIFO queueing; in queue mode worker concurrency is controlled separately but can be bounded by the same production limit variable.

n8n publishes a benchmark example with up to 220 executions/second on one instance and a multi-instance queue-mode benchmark using webhook workers, workers, database, main, and Redis; it notes performance varies by workflow, resources, and scaling configuration.
n8n AI tool calls can pause for human approval over configured channels, giving selective oversight for irreversible or compliance-sensitive actions.

n8n warns that unbounded JSON/binary payloads, node count, Code nodes, manual executions, and concurrent workflows can cause memory errors; mitigation includes chunking, avoiding Code nodes, sub-workflows, and memory sizing.
n8n AI workflow evaluation guidance distinguishes pre-deployment light evaluation from post-deployment metric-based evaluation and recommends regression datasets after bug fixes.

Temporal is a scalable durable-execution runtime; Event History records workflow state at each step so executions can resume, and applications can consist of millions to billions of workflow executions.

Temporal workflows are code-defined, can run for years, use Event History as source of truth, replay history to resume, require deterministic decisions, and isolate non-deterministic external effects in Activities whose results are recorded.
Temporal Activities are normal functions for single actions, may be non-deterministic, should be idempotent, and can use heartbeat details for checkpointing retries.

Temporal worker entities poll task queues; workers are stateless and can handle many open executions with latency tradeoffs; worker identity should map to execution context/log streams; workers execute code outside the Temporal Service.

Temporal task queues are lightweight on-demand queues polled by workers, support load balancing, task routing, throttling, persistence across worker outages, and guaranteed event ordering within a workflow history.
Camunda uses BPMN as a graphical notation for complex processes; Modeler supports BPMN 2.0 modeling, and service tasks require task type plus job workers.
Zeebe queues jobs until workers request them, supports retries/backoff/incidents, can reassign timed-out jobs, and is at-least-once so worker code must be idempotent.
Camunda incidents represent stuck process execution; resolution involves fixing data or retries and marking incident resolved so execution can continue.

Camunda process variables are global to the process instance by default; concurrent paths can race, so documentation recommends limited variable writes, output mappings, subprocess scopes, and minimum required variables.
Camunda Operate monitors and troubleshoots Zeebe process instances, resolves incidents, updates variables, retries/cancels many instances, and can modify active instances.

Argo Workflows is a Kubernetes-native, container-native workflow engine supporting DAG and step-based workflows, implemented as Kubernetes CRDs for parallel jobs, ML/data processing, and CI/CD on Kubernetes.
Argo WorkflowTemplates define reusable workflows in-cluster and can be managed by CLI, kubectl, GitOps via Argo CD, or UI.
Argo CronWorkflows schedule Workflow objects and include cron-specific options such as concurrencyPolicy and workflowSpec templates.
Argo supports retryStrategy with retry policies such as Always, OnFailure, OnError, and OnTransientError, plus expressions.
Argo workflows that use artifacts require an artifact repository; supported repositories include S3-compatible stores, GCS, Azure Blob, Git, HDFS, HTTP, and others.
Argo synchronization can limit parallel execution with mutexes, semaphores, and parallelism controls at workflow or template levels.

observed_strengths: Large low/no-code app/API integration surface
Self-host/cloud packaging with privacy positioning
Queue-mode split of main/webhook/worker roles with Redis and DB persistence
AI tool human-review channels and AI evaluation guidance
Published benchmark framework and example throughput numbers
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: Workflow PRD claims audit/Cedar/tenant advantages but lacks connector-catalog breadth targets
No explicit memory/large-payload bounds or artifact offload rule for workflow steps
AI workflow regression datasets and metric-based eval gates are not named
Webhook/main/worker split and health/metrics readiness are not encoded as acceptance criteria

measurable_patches.patch: Add connector catalog target with per-connector auth, quota, retry, and data-class metadata.
measurable_patches.measure: connector_catalog_min=100 GA connectors before public GA; every connector has auth/quota/retry/data_class metadata and source citation

measurable_patches.patch: Forbid unbounded in-memory JSON/binary payloads; require chunking or artifact references.
measurable_patches.measure: workflow_spec.v1 rejects steps without max_payload_bytes or artifact_ref for large payload classes

measurable_patches.patch: Add AI-workflow eval dataset + post-bug regression loop.
measurable_patches.measure: each AI-enabled workflow has eval_dataset_ref and regression_run_id before production enablement

reject_or_constrain: Do not adopt human approval as a required autonomy authority path; Oyatie can model human-review only as optional tenant business policy, not as agent-control authority.

observed_strengths: Durable execution via Event History
Replay-safe deterministic workflow code with external effects isolated in Activities
Idempotent activity/checkpoint guidance
Task queues with worker polling, routing, throttling, persisted tasks, and event ordering
Worker identity guidance linked to execution context/log streams
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: Workflow PRD has saga/idempotency but lacks a replay-safety class for every step
Worker identity, task routing, throttling, and queue persistence are not first-class product contract fields
Activity checkpoint/heartbeat equivalent is not named for long-running steps

measurable_patches.patch: Add replay_safety_class and side_effect_boundary for each step.
measurable_patches.measure: schema rejects external I/O in deterministic step class; side-effect steps require idempotency_key and activity_checkpoint_policy

measurable_patches.patch: Add event_history as the durable source of truth for workflow-instance resumption.
measurable_patches.measure: restart test proves zero lost progress and zero duplicate side effects across worker crash
every worker poller exports worker_id, queue_id, registered_step_types, capacity, throttle_state, and log_stream_ref

reject_or_constrain: Do not require user SDK code as the only workflow authoring path; Oyatie keeps canonical JSON spec plus generated adapters.

observed_strengths: BPMN-based business-readable modeling and Modeler UX
Zeebe job worker queue with retries/backoff/incidents
Incident lifecycle and Operate remediation UI
Variable-scope and concurrency guidance for parallel paths
Connectors/user tasks for human/business process integration
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: Workflow PRD forbids BPMN compatibility but does not preserve the business-readable process-view advantage
No incident lifecycle state machine for stuck execution
Variable race/scoping hazards are not explicit anti-patterns
Operate-like bulk retry/cancel/modify must be mapped to ops-managed safe controls, not manual troubleshooting

measurable_patches.patch: Add incident_resolution_state_machine for stuck workflow instances.
measurable_patches.measure: stuck execution emits incident_id, root_error_class, remediation_policy, retry_budget, and audit_chain row before retry/cancel

measurable_patches.patch: Forbid unscoped writes in parallel paths; require output mappings/minimum variable writes.
measurable_patches.measure: workflow_spec.v1 rejects parallel steps that write overlapping variables without merge_policy

measurable_patches.patch: Represent business-readable projection without making BPMN XML canonical.
measurable_patches.measure: roundtrip tests prove visual projection preserves canonical workflow_spec.v1 semantics

reject_or_constrain: Do not adopt BPMN XML as the canonical format; keep workflow_spec.v1 as source of truth.
Do not introduce manual incident SSH troubleshooting; remediation must be ops/API/audit-chain managed.

observed_strengths: Kubernetes-native CRD workflow engine
Container-native DAG/steps for parallel compute
Reusable WorkflowTemplates and GitOps management
CronWorkflow schedules/backfill patterns
RetryStrategy, artifact repository, and synchronization primitives
where_oyatie_lacks_or_is_underspecified: Workflow PRD says multi-domain and not K8s-only but lacks a clean container-job adapter boundary
Artifact repository and large output lifecycle are underspecified
Cron/backfill and schedule concurrency policies are not explicit
No semaphore/mutex/parallelism contract for shared external resources

measurable_patches.patch: Add container_job_adapter as one executor target, isolated from core workflow semantics.
measurable_patches.measure: Kubernetes executor is optional adapter; core spec validates without Kubernetes fields

measurable_patches.patch: Add artifact_ref lifecycle for large inputs/outputs and retention/data-class metadata.
measurable_patches.measure: large payload steps require artifact_ref with repository_class, retention_policy, digest, and data_class
cron/backfill steps require concurrency_policy; shared resource steps require mutex/semaphore/parallelism cap

reject_or_constrain: Do not make Kubernetes CRDs the product authority; they are an adapter projection only.
Do not require Argo CD/GitOps for every tenant runtime; Oyatie deployment authority remains OpenTofu/ops for infrastructure.

cross_competitor_patch_backlog: Add source-backed competitive_claim schema: competitor, evidence_refs, observed_strengths, oyatie_gap, patch_id, verification.
Add workflow_spec.v1 fields for replay_safety_class, side_effect_boundary, max_payload_bytes/artifact_ref, schedule_backfill_policy, and synchronization limits.
Add Rust validator that fails unsourced competitive claims and workflow steps with side effects but no idempotency/retry/checkpoint policy.
Add benchmark harness comparing Oyatie webhook/step throughput against n8n official benchmark shape without copying unsourced competitor claims.
Add incident lifecycle model with audit-chain remediation actions and no manual SSH troubleshooting path.
